claims.text: The target nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The nanoparticles are initially crystallized as a solid solution.
Preservation of the solid-solution structure governs maintenance of structural and chemical stability.
The absence of phase segregation or decomposition governs maintenance of structural and chemical stability.
In-situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy can provide real-time observation of structural and chemical changes under operating conditions.
The nanoparticles will remain structurally and chemically stable if the solid-solution structure is preserved and segregation or decomposition does not occur.
The proposed prediction is intended to apply from 473 to 1923 K.
Phase segregation or decomposition within the operating range is designated as a falsifying observation.
A significant change in chemical composition within the operating range is designated as a falsifying observation.

contradictions.description: The prediction is conditional on preservation of the solid solution and absence of segregation or decomposition. Observing segregation or decomposition merely makes that condition false rather than logically falsifying the conditional prediction.
